claims.text: Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled low-temperature annealing will produce a bimodal fine-and-coarse grain structure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
A bimodal grain structure will improve the tensile ductility and uniform elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The bimodal microstructure can improve ductility without significantly reducing yield or compressive strength.
The intervention will preserve impact-triggered chemical energy release.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal compressive strain of approximately 13.5%.
The tensile ductility of HfZrTiTa0.53 is presumed to be low and lower than its reported compressive terminal strain.
Fine-grain regions retain high strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Coarse-grain regions enhance tensile strain accommodation through grain-boundary sliding.
Larger grains facilitate dislocation motion and delay tensile necking.
Dislocation-mediated plasticity and strain hardening can support a combination of high strength and high uniform elongation in a grain-refined multicomponent alloy.
Tensile uniform elongation will reach at least 20%.
Yield and compressive strength will decline by less than 10% after processing.
Annealing at excessive temperature may cause uncontrolled grain coarsening or phase decomposition that diminishes strength.
The proposed tensile response applies at room temperature under quasi-static loading at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
Preservation of the proposed behavior extends to dynamic loading at strain rates comparable to impact tests.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome describes tensile uniform elongation as improving from approximately 13.5%, but the baseline explicitly identifies 13.5% as terminal strain measured in compression and states that tensile ductility is unknown. Compression terminal strain is therefore used inconsistently as a tensile uniform-elongation baseline.
The hypothesis characterizes the 786 MPa yield strength as high, whereas the material-initial-state field characterizes it as moderate.
